Description: Smooth scrolling to in-page anchors is optional; when used it must stop for people who request reduced motion
Do: Enable smooth scrolling only inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference query
Don't: Force animated scrolling on users who asked for reduced motion
Code Example Bad: html { scroll-behavior: smooth; } with no reduced-motion check

Description: A fixed or sticky header must not hide anchor targets or the focused element (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured)
Do: Offset scroll targets by the header height and check focused fields are not covered
Don't: Let nav overlap first section content
Code Example Bad: Sticky header covering anchor targets and focused inputs

Description: The current page or section should be identifiable visually and programmatically
Do: Mark the current item with a visible indicator and aria-current
Don't: Rely on color alone or give no indication of the current location
Code Example Bad: All navigation links styled identically with no aria-current

Description: Users expect back to work predictably
Do: Preserve navigation history properly

Description: URLs should reflect current state for sharing
Do: Update URL on state/view changes

Description: Show user location in site hierarchy
Do: Use for sites with 3+ levels of depth

Description: Too many animations cause distraction and motion sickness
Do: Animate only where motion explains a change of state, place, or relationship
Don't: Animate elements purely for decoration or attention
Code Example Good: One transition showing where newly added content came from
Code Example Bad: Several elements bouncing or pulsing at the same time

Description: No duration or easing curve is universally correct; motion timing should follow the size, distance, and purpose of the change
Do: Review duration and easing in the rendered interaction on target devices and keep them consistent within a component family
Don't: Copy one preset duration or curve onto every transition without reviewing it
Code Example Good: Named motion tokens reviewed in context, with a reduced-motion alternative
Code Example Bad: The same long transition applied to every state change

Description: Respect the user's motion preference, including for parallax and scroll-linked effects that can cause discomfort
Do: Check prefers-reduced-motion and provide a static or minimal alternative
Don't: Force parallax, scroll-jacking, or large movement regardless of the preference

Description: Show system status during waits users notice
Do: Use a skeleton, spinner, or progress indicator; prefer determinate progress when the duration is known
Don't: Leave the UI frozen or blank with no feedback
Code Example Good: Skeleton matching the incoming layout on a region marked aria-busy='true'

Description: Hover effects don't work on touch devices
Do: Use click/tap for primary interactions
Don't: Rely only on hover for important actions

Description: Moving content that starts automatically, lasts more than five seconds, and runs alongside other content needs a way to pause, stop, or hide it (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2)
Do: Reserve continuous animation for indicators such as loading, and stop it when the work ends
Code Example Good: Spinner shown only while the request is pending

Description: Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints
Do: Use transform and opacity for animations

Description: Stacking context conflicts cause hidden elements
Do: Define a small set of named stacking layers (for example dropdown, sticky, modal, toast) in one place

Description: Hidden overflow can clip important content
Do: Test all content fits within containers

Description: Fixed elements can overlap or be inaccessible
Do: Account for safe areas and other fixed elements
Code Example Good: Fixed nav + fixed bottom with gap

Description: New stacking contexts reset z-index
Do: Understand what creates new stacking context
Don't: Expect z-index to work across contexts

Description: Layout shift when content loads is jarring
Do: Reserve space for async content

Description: 100vh can be problematic on mobile browsers
Do: Use dvh or account for mobile browser chrome

Description: Very long lines of running text are hard to read; WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.8 (AAA) asks that line width not exceed 80 characters (40 for CJK)
Do: Limit the measure of running text and check it with the real typeface and content
Don't: Let text span full viewport width

Description: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) requires pointer targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels unless spacing or another exception applies; SC 2.5.5 (AAA) uses 44 by 44 CSS pixels. Platform guidance for touch is larger: Apple's Human Interface Guidelines recommend at least 44 by 44 pt and Material Design at least 48 by 48 dp
Do: Treat 24 by 24 CSS px as the web floor and size touch controls to the platform guidance
Don't: Present 44 px as the WCAG AA rule or ship targets under 24 by 24 CSS px without the spacing exception
Code Example Bad: A 16 by 16 px icon button with no padding

Description: Adjacent targets need separation so they are not activated by mistake; under WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 an undersized target passes only if a 24 CSS px circle centered on it does not overlap another target or another undersized target's circle
Do: Leave visible space between adjacent actions, especially undersized ones
Code Example Good: Adjacent icon buttons separated by a gap
Code Example Bad: Small targets touching edge to edge

Description: Custom gestures can conflict with system
Do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content

Description: Accidental refresh is frustrating
Do: Disable where not needed

Description: Tactile feedback improves interaction feel
Do: Use for confirmations and important actions

Description: Keyboard users need a visible focus indicator (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7); the indicator should contrast with adjacent colors (SC 1.4.11)
Do: Use visible focus rings on interactive elements

Description: Visual feedback on interactive elements
Do: Change cursor and add subtle visual change
Don't: No hover feedback on clickable elements
Code Example Bad: Clickable rows with no hover or cursor change

Description: Controls should acknowledge a press or click immediately
Do: Give buttons and other controls a visible pressed state

Description: Disabled controls are exempt from contrast minimums but must still be distinguishable from enabled ones
Do: Use the disabled state with a distinct style, and say nearby why an action is unavailable
Code Example Good: <button disabled> with a distinct style and a short reason next to it

Description: Prevent double submission during async actions
Do: Disable button and show loading state

Description: Users need to know when something fails
Do: Show clear error messages near problem
Code Example Good: Error text tied to the field with aria-describedby, plus an icon or border change

Description: Confirm successful actions to users
Do: Show a brief success message or visible state change

Description: Prevent accidental destructive actions
Do: Confirm before delete/irreversible actions

Description: Text needs at least 4.5:1 contrast, or 3:1 for large text (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3, AA); UI component boundaries and meaningful graphics need 3:1 (SC 1.4.11)
Do: Measure the actual rendered foreground and background pair
Don't: Judge contrast by eye or from token names
Code Example Bad: Light gray body text approved by eye

Description: Don't convey information by color alone (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1)
Do: Use icons/text in addition to color

Description: Images need text alternatives
Do: Descriptive alt text for meaningful images

Description: Screen readers use headings for navigation
Do: Use sequential heading levels h1-h6
Don't: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling

Description: Interactive elements need accessible names
Do: Add aria-label for icon-only buttons

Description: All functionality must be operable by keyboard (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1) in a meaningful order (SC 2.4.3)
Do: Keep DOM order aligned with visual order; use tabindex='0' only for custom interactive widgets
Don't: Positive tabindex values, keyboard traps, or unreachable controls
Code Example Good: Source order that matches the visual reading order
Code Example Bad: tabindex='3' to force a custom tab sequence

Description: Content should make sense when read aloud
Do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly

Description: Every input needs a visible label that is programmatically associated with it
Do: Use a label element with for/id or wrap the input; keep the label visible

Description: Error messages must be announced
Do: Use aria-live or role=alert for errors

Description: Allow keyboard users to skip navigation
Do: Provide skip to main content link
Don't: No skip link on nav-heavy pages
Code Example Bad: Dozens of tab stops before the main content

Description: Large images slow page load
Do: Serve appropriately sized images in an efficient format (for example AVIF or WebP with a fallback)

Description: Load content as needed
Do: Lazy load below-fold images and content

Description: Large bundles slow initial load
Do: Split code by route/feature

Description: Repeat visits should be fast
Do: Set appropriate cache headers

Description: Web fonts can hide text while loading and shift layout when they arrive
Do: Use font-display (swap or optional) and a metric-matched fallback face
Don't: Invisible text during load or a large reflow when the font swaps in
Code Example Good: font-display: swap with a fallback @font-face using size-adjust
Code Example Bad: No font-display and an unrelated fallback font

Description: External scripts can block rendering
Do: Load non-critical scripts async/defer

Description: Large JavaScript slows interaction
Do: Monitor and minimize bundle size

Description: CSS/JS can block first paint
Do: Inline critical CSS defer non-critical

Description: Errors should appear near the problem
Do: Show error below related input
Don't: Single error message at top of form

Description: Validate as user types or on blur
Do: Validate on blur for most fields

Description: Use appropriate input types
Do: Use email tel number url etc

Description: Help browsers autofill correctly
Do: Use autocomplete attribute properly

Description: Mark required fields clearly
Do: Use asterisk or (required) text

Description: Let users see password while typing
Do: Toggle to show/hide password

Description: Confirm form submission status
Do: Show loading then success/error state

Description: Inputs should look interactive
Do: Use distinct input styling
Don't: Inputs that look like plain text

Description: Show appropriate keyboard for input type
Do: Use inputmode attribute

Description: Design for mobile then enhance for larger
Do: Start with mobile styles then add breakpoints

Description: Test across content-driven breakpoints, including narrow widths and zoom
Do: Check layouts at 320 CSS px width (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow), at 200% text size, and while resizing continuously
Don't: Check only the developer's own screen size
Code Example Good: Continuous resize plus zoom checks in the browser
Code Example Bad: One device size checked before release

Description: Mobile layouts need touch-sized targets
Do: Increase touch targets on mobile

Description: Text must stay readable and resize to 200% without loss of content or function (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4)
Do: Use relative units and test at larger text sizes; iOS Safari zooms into form fields whose font size is below 16px
Don't: Tiny body text or sizes that ignore the user's font settings
Code Example Good: font-size in rem; inputs at 1rem or larger
Code Example Bad: Body text fixed at a small px size

Description: Set viewport for mobile devices
Do: Use width=device-width initial-scale=1

Description: Content should reflow without two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px width (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10)
Do: Ensure content fits viewport width
Code Example Good: Fix the overflowing element; overflow-wrap: anywhere for long strings
Code Example Bad: overflow-x: hidden on body masking content that no longer fits

Description: Images should scale with container
Do: Use max-width: 100% on images

Description: Tables can overflow on mobile
Do: Use horizontal scroll or card layout

Description: Line height affects readability; WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 requires content to keep working when users raise line height to 1.5 times the font size
Do: Choose line height for the typeface and measure, and verify text survives the SC 1.4.12 spacing overrides
Don't: Fixed-height text containers that clip when spacing increases
Code Example Good: Text containers that grow with their content
Code Example Bad: height: fixed on a paragraph box

Description: Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning
Do: Use consistent modular scale
Code Example Good: A named type scale defined once and reused

Description: Headings should stand out from body
Do: Clear size/weight difference

Description: Guide users when no content exists
Do: Show helpful message and action

Description: Help users recover from errors
Do: Provide clear next steps

Description: Show progress for multi-step processes
Do: Step indicators or progress bar

Description: Transient messages suit non-critical confirmations; anything users must act on or reread needs persistent UI
Do: Give users enough time to read toasts (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.1), announce them with a polite live region, and keep errors and undo actions available elsewhere
Don't: Put the only copy of an error or an undo action in a toast that disappears quickly
Code Example Good: Polite live-region toast plus a persistent record of the change
Code Example Bad: Error shown only in a short-lived toast

Description: Handle long content gracefully
Do: Truncate with ellipsis and expand option

Description: Use locale-appropriate date formats
Do: Use relative or locale-aware dates

Description: Format large numbers for readability
Do: Use thousand separators or abbreviations

Description: Show realistic placeholders during dev
Do: Use realistic sample data

Description: Users should be able to skip tutorials
Do: Provide Skip and Back buttons

Description: Help users find results faster
Do: Show predictions as user types

Description: Dead ends frustrate users
Do: Show 'No results' with suggestions

Description: Editing one by one is tedious
Do: Allow multi-select and bulk edit

Description: Users need to know they talk to AI
Do: Clearly label AI generated content

Description: Waiting for full text is slow
Do: Stream long responses as they are generated and announce completion to assistive technology
Don't: Show only a spinner until a long response finishes, or announce every token
Code Example Good: Streamed text with a polite completion announcement
Code Example Bad: Spinner until the whole response is ready

Description: Elements should respond to eye tracking before pinch
Do: Scale/highlight element on look

Description: Spatial content must stay legible and separated from the user's surroundings
Do: Keep content in system-provided windows and volumes; use depth offsets sparingly to separate layers
Don't: Opaque full-field panels that block the user's view of their surroundings
Code Example Good: WindowGroup content using the system window background

Description: Autoplaying video consumes data and energy; moving media that starts automatically needs a pause control (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2)
Do: Click-to-play or pause when off-screen

Description: Heavy 3D/Image assets increase carbon footprint
Do: Compress and lazy load 3D models
Don't: Load uncompressed multi-megabyte textures up front

Description: AI needs user feedback to improve
Do: Offer thumbs up/down or a Regenerate action

Description: Infinite scrolling suits continuous, undirected browsing of homogeneous content; pagination or a Load more control suits finding a specific item, comparing items, and returning to a known position (Nielsen Norman Group, 2022)
Do: Choose from the user's task; if content loads continuously, restore scroll position on Back, keep the footer reachable, keep the position addressable in the URL, and announce newly loaded items
Don't: Default to infinite scroll for search results or catalogs that people compare and revisit
Code Example Good: Paginated or Load more results with URL state (?page=3) and restored scroll position
Code Example Bad: Endless feed that loses position on Back and hides the footer
